primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: The partial database removal provision created by Public Chapter 268 of 2025. It answers the mixed-count case where some counts were dismissed as part of a plea and others produced a conviction.
The non-conviction grounds, against which each count in the schedule is identified.
The court forwards the order to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation within 30 days of entry.

counselFlags: Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it.

No official Tennessee participant form exists. Both state form indices were inspected directly and neither publishes an expunction form of any kind; this is a negative finding established from the authoritative index, not a failure to search. A controlled custom instrument is therefore the only available strategy, and it is not represented as an official form.

Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025 and codified by Public Chapter 608 effective 2026-03-25, and clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering — the state's own expunction page still reasons from a section that has been nothing but definitions since 2025-04-24. A petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet carries the current citation and instructs the participant to confirm it with the clerk or the district attorney general before filing.
Tennessee expunction reaches no federal, military, tribal or out-of-state record, and a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on a clearance check.

The governing section prescribes no caption form and no contents for the participant's instrument. The caption follows the ordinary criminal-case style of the court having jurisdiction, with the filer designated as the source designates them. What individual clerks and courts in fact expect is not established and no county practice was surveyed; the caption is a visual- and counsel-review item.

This is partial removal, not expunction of the case. The counts that produced the conviction are untouched and are eligible only through the conviction analysis, if at all. A participant who expects the whole case cleared is a stop condition.

Whether the relief reaches paper records or only electronic databases was not established, and the source flags that limitation as materially changing what a participant gets. The packet withholds any assertion about paper coverage. A participant who needs the paper file cleared is a stop condition.

Whether any fee applies to a partial removal was not confirmed. The no-cost provision is framed around the non-conviction grounds and whether it reaches a partial removal in a mixed case is unresolved. No figure is quoted.
The count-by-count disposition schedule is a manual-completion item taken from the clerk's record. Where the dispositions cannot be established from that record, self-help stops.

The state control number is a manual-completion item read from the participant's own criminal history. It stays a bracket in generated output; the order cannot be completed without it, and the participant is told to capture it early.

The shared renderer's fixed section heading "VI. VERIFICATION" is a Pennsylvania-derived artefact of the frozen renderer contract, not a Tennessee drafting choice. Nothing in the governing section requires verification. This is a visual- and counsel-review item.
No fee figure is quoted anywhere in this packet. The source records no retrievable amount, and the filing-fee field is left null rather than filled with a circulating number.
No fee-waiver instrument is included and the fee-waiver field is left null, because the source establishes no waiver mechanism for this route.
The governing section states no waiting period. None is pleaded, none is imported from a neighbouring section, and the waiting-period field is left null.

Notarization is not prescribed by the governing section and no verification statute exists to cite, so verificationStatute.citation is left null and the signature block carries no penalty citation. County practice may differ, and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk.

Self-help stop conditions: Any dispute with the district attorney general about eligibility, or any indication the office will oppose. Any other conviction anywhere on the record, including federal and out-of-state convictions that would be ineligible in Tennessee. Unpaid court costs, fines or restitution, which mean the sentence is not complete. Any DUI, sexual offence or registration matter. Any domestic violence or child-victim offence. Federal, military, tribal or out-of-state records, which Tennessee expunction does not reach. Immigration consequences, and any security-clearance question. Any question that turns on whether the county clerk uses the pre-2025 or the reorganized section numbering. The participant expects the whole case cleared. This remedy leaves the conviction in place. The count-by-count dispositions cannot be established from the clerk's record. The participant needs the paper file cleared and not only the electronic databases, which is the limitation that was not resolved.

provenance.registryExcerpt: The controlling review identified this remedy from a secondary profile and left its citation unresolved as the highest-value Tennessee research item. It is resolved: Public Chapter 268 of 2025 created a partial database removal provision at T.C.A. § 40-32-106(c)(2), and the TBI's own form BI-0334, revision 04/2025, is captioned Removal of Criminal Offender Record pursuant to T.C.A. § 40-32-106(c)(2), which corroborates both the citation and the mechanism from an official source. The remedy answers the most common real-world Tennessee scenario after a clean dismissal: a multi-count case where some counts were dismissed as part of a plea and others produced a conviction. Whether the relief reaches paper records or only electronic databases was not established, and the review flags that limitation as materially changing what a participant gets. Venue: Statewide statute with originating-court venue. The petition goes to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action — the county criminal, circuit or general sessions court where the case originated. A person with cases in several counties files separately in each. There is no statewide participant form, so what varies locally is the clerk's own paperwork: the AOC directs filers to check with the court clerk because separate forms may be required for multiple charges. Destination: The county criminal, circuit or general sessions court having jurisdiction in the previous action — Confirmed on 2026-08-06 by direct inspection of both Tennessee AOC form indices: the self-help forms page publishes only divorce and order-of-protection forms, and the full forms-and-publications inventory covers appellate, divorce, general sessions civil, mediation, non-IV-D child support, order of protection, parenting plan and trial court forms, plus licensing forms. No expunction form appears in either. This is a negative finding established by inspection of the authoritative index, not by failure to search. filing: A motion to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action, filed with that court's clerk, under the existing docket rather than as a new case. fees: Not established for the partial removal itself. The § 40-32-106(a) no-cost provision is framed around removal and destruction of the public records of a person who has been charged, and whether it reaches a (c)(2) partial removal in a mixed case was not confirmed. No figure is quoted. feeWaiver: Not established for this route. notice: The clerk serves the motion on the district attorney general in the ordinary course. service: Through the clerk. The participant does not effect service. participantSignature: The petitioner signs the motion. notarization: Not prescribed. Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing. Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it. No reach to federal records; a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on clearance checks. This is partial removal, not expunction of the case. The counts that produced the conviction are untouched, and on the current record the relief is established for electronic databases with paper coverage unconfirmed. Exclusion: A case in which no count resulted in a conviction, which routes to the ordinary free non-conviction petition and gets the fuller remedy. Exclusion: The counts that produced the conviction. Those are untouched by this route and are eligible only through the conviction-expunction analysis, if at all. Exclusion: Any expectation of full expunction. This is partial removal of the non-conviction counts, and on the current record it reaches electronic databases with paper coverage unconfirmed. Waiting period — Statutory waiting period: None identified for the partial removal itself. Waiting period — TBI transmission: The court sends the order to the TBI within 30 days of entry.
